2025_139_m121724bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of December 17, 2024, held at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, with Vice President Anne presiding in the absence of President Schmidt and Dr. Wilson. The Board approved a four-item consent agenda and awarded two playground contracts payable from the 2023 Capital Projects Fund: $2,566,375.57 for equipment and installation and $3,767,447.16 for site work, landscaping, asphalt paving and contingency. The meeting also served as a farewell to Secretary Gary N. Hauff, who noted he had served on the Troy School Board for almost 26 years.
2025_139_m121724bdmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, December 17, 2024, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. Vice President Anne called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and adjourned it at 8:36 p.m.

**Attendance**
Present with Mrs. Anne: Alic, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart. Absent: President Schmidt, Dr. Wilson. Also present: Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Pagel, Burden, Trudell. Approximately 75 members of the audience attended.

**Recognition — American Red Cross / Athens High School blood drives**
Athens High School was selected to be honored by the American Red Cross for hosting blood drives in its community. Carmen Timm of the American Red Cross recognized teachers Shawn DuFresne and Deanna Fakhouri and students Claire Kilbride, Maggie Ianev, Everett Marshall, Willow Bodendorfer and Jack Appledorn, who ran blood drives to earn scholarship money.

**Mission Moment — Global Leadership Summit, Berlin**
Troy High Colts who attended the Global Leadership Summit in Berlin, Germany were recognized. They travelled to the French Riviera, Switzerland and Berlin exploring the Impact of Water on Society, among 1,100 students from around the world. Communications Instructor and summit adviser Harriet Clark introduced the students.

**Student Spotlight and student representatives**
Ryan Stasinski, an Athens High School senior in the TSD Creative Guild, was spotlighted; Thomas Butcher presented his work. Reports came from Nurayda Albeez (International Academy-East), Kristian Vitanovich (Troy College and Career High School), Madie Miller (Troy High School, filling in for Adam McManus) and Diana D'Aloisio (Athens High School).

**Consent agenda**
Moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Mr. Haupt, approving items A-D: minutes of the November 12, 2024 Workshop; minutes of the November 19, 2024 Board Meeting; Treasurer's Report for October 2024; Budget Amendment #1. Yes: 5. No: 0. Absent: Schmidt, Wilson.

**Business — Playground Equipment Purchase Phase 2**
Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Alic, awarding the bid for playground equipment and installation as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Yes: 5. No: 0. Absent: Schmidt, Wilson.

| Award | Vendor | Amount |

| Contingency | | | $279,070.16 |
| **Total** | | | **$3,767,447.16** |

**Other agenda categories**
Additions and Deletions: none. Public Communication on agenda items: none. Personnel: none. Curriculum: none. Other: none.

**Public communication (non-agenda items)**
Seven community members addressed the Board. No action was taken by the Board.

**Board comments and announcements**
Board members thanked Mr. Hauff for his dedication and years of service, and welcomed incoming members Audra Melton, Ayesha Potts and Stephanie Zendler. Mr. Hauff said he was happy to have served on the Troy School Board for almost 26 years. Mrs. Anne announced the next Board Workshop at Baker Middle School on January 14th at 6:00 p.m., and the Organizational and Regular Board Meeting on January 21st in the Services Building at 7:00 p.m. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education.

**Identification**
Official minutes of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan — Board Meeting of December 17, 2024, held at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. The minutes carry the notation GH/jh and are signed "Respectfully submitted, Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education."

**Call to order and roll**
Vice President Anne called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mrs. Anne, present were Board members Alic, Hauff, Haupt and Philippart. President Schmidt and Dr. Wilson were absent. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Pagel, Burden and Trudell. There were approximately 75 members of the audience.

**Recognition — American Red Cross, Athens High School blood drives**
The Board recognized Athens High School, which had been selected to be honored by the American Red Cross for its support in hosting blood drives in the community. Carmen Timm of the American Red Cross attended to recognize Athens teachers Shawn DuFresne and Deanna Fakhouri and their students, who were running blood drives during the school year to earn scholarship money. The students called forward to receive recognition for their efforts were Claire Kilbride, Maggie Ianev, Everett Marshall, Willow Bodendorfer and Jack Appledorn.

**Mission Moment — Troy High School students at the Global Leadership Summit in Berlin, Germany**
The Board recognized Troy High Colts who attended the Global Leadership Summit in Berlin, Germany during the past summer. The students, selected on leadership and outstanding character, travelled to the French Riviera, Switzerland and Berlin exploring the Impact of Water on Society in an attempt to better understand water's influence on transportation, agriculture, energy and more. They were part of 1,100 students from around the world studying water's impact in other European countries. During the summit, students were placed in teams and charged with solving a global problem related to the theme of water; using design thinking, they ideated and created a prototype to solve their problem and presented a one-minute pitch on the prototype to the judges. Communications Instructor and Global Leadership Summit Adviser Harriet Clark was invited to share more about the competition and introduce her students. Harriett Clark recognized the following students: Ashley Carron, Anusha Gupta, Ava Fleming, Jake Baker, Josie Lido, Katerina Zak, Kate Bestul, Vivian Edoff, Nicole Gherase, Laith Hermiz, Nainika Jasti, Keira McComb, Shreyan Maini, Maya Saad, Neel Nagappala and Tia Tonelli.

**Student Spotlight**
The Student Spotlight recognizes the talents and achievements of students in the TSD Creative Guild. The spotlight was shone on Ryan Stasinski, a senior from Athens High School with a unique passion for sports. Thomas Butcher attended to describe the work.

**Reports from High School Student Representatives**
Nurayda Albeez, student representative for International Academy-East, reported on events and activities at her school. Kristian Vitanovich, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, reported on events and activities at TCCHS. Madie Miller, student representative for Troy High School, filled in for Adam McManus, who was not present, and reported on events and activities at her school. Diana D'Aloisio, student representative for Athens High School, reported on events and activities at Athens.

**Additions and Deletions; Public Communication (agenda items)**
Additions and Deletions: none. Public Communication on agenda items: none.

**General — Consent Agenda**
It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Troy Board of Education take action to approve items A, B, C and D on the consent agenda. The items were: minutes of the November 12, 2024 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the November 19, 2024 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report for October 2024; and Budget Amendment #1. The vote was Yes: 5, No: 0, Absent: Schmidt, Wilson.

**Personnel and Curriculum**
No Personnel items were presented. No Curriculum items were presented.

**Business — Playground Equipment Purchase Phase 2**
It was moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Alic that the bid for playground equipment and installation be awarded as set out below and that the amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund.

| Award | Vendor | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Playground Equipment, Contractor #2 | Midstate Rec/Playworld | $1,320,079.97 |

The vote was Yes: 5, No: 0, Absent: Schmidt, Wilson.

It was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Alic that the bid for playground site work be awarded as set out below and that the amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. The vote was Yes: 5, No: 0, Absent: Schmidt, Wilson. Together with the Phase 2 equipment award adopted earlier in the same meeting, both playground actions were charged to the 2023 Capital Projects Fund.

**Public Communication (non-agenda items)**
Seven community members addressed the Board during public communication. No action was taken by the Board.

**Other**
No items were presented under Other.

**Board Comments**
Board members shared sentiments about Mr. Hauff and thanked him for his dedication and years of service as a board member to the Troy School District students and community. Board members also congratulated Audra Melton, Ayesha Potts and Stephanie Zendler and welcomed them to the Troy Board of Education. Mr. Hauff shared his sentiments on how happy he was to have served on the Troy School Board for almost 26 years and acknowledged his appreciation for many members of the Troy School District team.

**Announcements**
Mrs. Anne announced that the next Board Workshop would be held at Baker Middle School on January 14th at 6:00 p.m., and that the Organizational and Regular Board Meeting would be held on January 21st in the Services Building at 7:00 p.m.

**Adjournment**
The meeting adjourned at 8:36 p.m.
